summary.headline: Carborundum Universal FY26 standalone sales rose 8.6% to INR 3,024 crore, while consolidated PBIT fell 25.3% to INR 404 crore on subsidiary losses.
summary.overview: Standalone performance rebounded through H2 FY26, with Q4 sales up 23.1% YoY to INR 845 crore and Q4 PAT more than doubling to INR 122 crore. Consolidated sales crossed INR 5,000 crore (INR 5,149 crore, +6.5%), but consolidated PBT before exceptions fell 27.2% to INR 416 crore, driven by VAW sanctions, Foskor, Awuko and Rhodius losses. Management decided to wind down Awuko and to close Foskor Zirconia, booking exceptional items of INR 135 crore in FY26. FY27 guidance is for about 4-4.5% consolidated sales growth, which falls to 11-12% excluding Foskor and Awuko, with capex of about INR 400 crore.

segments.name: Standalone Abrasives
segments.commentary: FY26 sales INR 1,270 crore (+6.2%); H1 down 2.8% to INR 594 crore, H2 up 15.6% YoY to INR 675 crore. PBIT INR 195 crore (+0.9%), margin 15.3% vs 16.1%.

segments.name: Standalone Electrominerals
segments.commentary: FY26 sales INR 906 crore (+11.1%), with exports up 100% to over 33% of sales. PBIT rose 31.1% to INR 82 crore; management said growth was mainly volume with price roughly flat.

segments.name: Standalone Ceramics
segments.commentary: FY26 sales INR 1,000 crore (+6.5%). PBIT fell 8% to INR 214 crore. Wear ceramics de-grew 9%; engineering ceramics grew 30% on SOFC demand; metallized cylinders grew 9% after a H1 production issue.

segments.name: Consolidated Abrasives
segments.commentary: FY26 sales INR 2,271 crore (+5.1%); Q4 INR 610 crore (+13.4% YoY). PBIT margin 4.3% vs 7.0%, with Rhodius loss about INR 45 crore and Awuko loss about INR 75 crore.

segments.name: Consolidated Electrominerals
segments.commentary: FY26 sales INR 1,632 crore (+3.7%), held back by VAW Russia sales down 35% in roubles. Foskor losses hit PBIT; consolidated segment PBIT INR 91 crore vs INR 177 crore.

segments.name: Consolidated Ceramics
segments.commentary: FY26 sales INR 1,268 crore (+9.3%); reported margin 20.2%. Industrial ceramics INR 569 crore (+7.8%); refractories and anti-corrosives INR 437 crore (+4.7%).

segments.name: Rhodius (Germany)
segments.commentary: FY26 sales EUR 61 million, down 8.8% from EUR 67 million, after about EUR 5 million lost to a Q1 logistics transition. PAT loss EUR 2.6 million vs EUR 0.2 million in FY25.

segments.name: Awuko
segments.commentary: Sales EUR 10.5 million (+4.6%); loss before tax rose to EUR 7.7 million. Voluntary winding-up started in Germany.

segments.name: VAW Russia
segments.commentary: Sales about 6 billion roubles vs 9.4 billion (-35.3%) under US sanctions; profit before tax 617 million roubles vs 1.7 billion, but still profitable.

segments.name: Foskor Zirconia (South Africa)
segments.commentary: Sales ZAR 461 million (+11.2%); loss before tax ZAR 77 million vs ZAR 37 million. Operations being discontinued as not commercially viable.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated sales growth of about 4-4.5%; about 11-12% excluding Foskor Zirconia and Awuko (together INR 343 crore of FY26 sales).
FY27 standalone Abrasives growth about 12% per management; consolidated Abrasives sales +5.5-6% (11-12% excluding Awuko).
FY27 consolidated Ceramics growth of 15-15.5%; consolidated Electrominerals sales -6.5% to -7% due to Foskor closure (8-9% excluding Foskor).
Margin guidance FY27: Abrasives 9.5-10% (FY26 comparable 7.9%), Ceramics 20.5-21% (reported 20.2%), Electrominerals 9-9.5% (comparable FY26 9.1%).
FY27 capex of about INR 400 crore, mainly advanced ceramics for power electronics, brown-fused alumina expansion, a 110 kV substation and a tunnel kiln for refractories.
Rhodius expected to grow sales about 5% in FY27 with a very small loss; Aspiration 2030 targets were not formally quantified.
capex_capacity: Consolidated capex FY26 INR 309 crore (standalone INR 235 crore) against INR 350 crore guided earlier.
Semiconductor wafer fab equipment components facility: first module commissioned in H1 FY26 at INR 66 crore; serial supplies start FY27, material revenue expected from 2029.
Aerospace and defence ceramics facility at INR 49 crore; STANAG 4 vehicle armour qualification secured; SCOMET approval awaited.
White fused alumina furnace upgrade from 2 MVA to 4.5 MVA at about INR 53 crore, adding up to INR 95 crore revenue potential; treatment facility INR 30 crore for up to INR 120 crore revenue.
Thin wheel capacity at Hosur using DRONCO-acquired assets: INR 83 crore outlay, 46 million wheels, peak revenue about INR 120 crore.
Refractories fired capacity to rise 75%; metallized cylinder capacity to be expanded in three phases over 18-24 months.
demand_pricing: Standalone H2 FY26 growth was broad-based, with Abrasives, Ceramics and Electrominerals each up double digits sequentially. Management attributed part of the rebound to GST rationalisation and festive demand.
China cut its abrasive export rebate from 9% to 0% from April 2026 (one analyst cited 13%). Management called it good for domestic industry but too recent to show in numbers.
Electrominerals growth was mainly volume; price roughly flat. Chinese import intensity has not declined.

Ceramics growth of 9.3% missed the 13-14% guided earlier, mainly due to deferred projects, especially in the glass segment. Management attributes the 15% FY27 outlook to backlog and customer forecasts.
Over 80% of Ceramics sales are exports; under 10% of Abrasives sales are exports.

qa_highlights.question: How large can the SOFC ceramics business become, and what is the wallet share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give wallet share but said it is an important supplier, with customer visibility to about 2028, and it expects a meaningful share of revenue as the engineered segment grows.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Ceramics growth miss the 13-14% guidance, and does it signal structural competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed mainly deferred projects, not structural change, and expects the 15% FY27 growth to be backed by backlog and customer forecasts.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for semiconductor fab-equipment ceramics revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Material qualification takes four to six years; samples are tested and serial production starts, with material revenue expected from 2029 onwards.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path to profitability at Rhodius?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects sales growth of 6-7% with the one-time EUR 5 million logistics loss not recurring, plus a special profitability programme, to return it to a small loss or breakeven in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Are there alternatives to Russian silicon carbide supply from VAW?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said replacing the capacity would be costly and difficult; it awaits sanctions relief and has no alternative for now.

risks_watch: Foskor Zirconia closure needs approvals in South Africa; the Awuko winding-up is ongoing in Germany.
VAW Russia sales are constrained by US sanctions, with no alternative supply route identified.
FY27 consolidated growth of 4-4.5% is low versus the 11-12% comparable figure, so the reported drop from exits needs watching.
Ceramics growth depends on the timing of deferred projects and on the US business, where exports fell 40% in FY26 for wear ceramics.
Rhodius returning to breakeven depends on recovering the lost EUR 5 million in sales and on cost actions.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the standalone rebound and balance sheet (net debt-free, debt-equity 0.08), but defensive on subsidiary losses and missed Ceramics guidance. Management avoided quantifying Aspiration 2030 targets and declined to disclose SOFC wallet share.
